articles.title: NFL injury tracker Week 3: Latest news, fantasy implications as Sam Darnold (glute) 'ready to go', Caleb Williams (hamstring) ruled out, Puka Nacua (hip) unlikely to play
articles.summary: Here's everything you need to know injury-wise for Week 3 of the NFL season.
articles.body: Week 3 is underway, and we're tracking all the injuries heading into the weekend.Jump to a team:AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | JetsAFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | SteelersAFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | TitansAFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | ChargersNFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | CommandersNFC North: Bears | Lions | Packers (played Thurs.) | VikingsNFC South: Falcons (played Thurs.) | Panthers | Saints | BuccaneersNFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | SeahawksLive injury updatesThe Seattle Seahawks will have their No. 1 quarterback on Sunday when they take on the Washington Commanders. Sam Darnold, who suffered a glute injury during the opening game of the season, was back at practice on Thursday as a full participant, and was off the injury report on Friday.In Darnold's absence, Drew Lock threw for 187 yards and a touchdown during Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. He followed that up during last week's win over the Arizona Cardinals with 235 passing yards and three touchdowns.Head coach Mike Macdonald had said Darnold is "on a good track right now" to play in Week 3; on Friday, he said that Darnold is "ready to go."Caleb Williams (hamstring) has been ruled out and Tyson Bagent (concussion) is questionable to play Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles. Williams left Week 2 with the injury and is considered week-to-week. Bagent practiced on Saturday, but remains in concussion protocol as part of the process. Case Keenum will either start or serve as Bagent's backup.Other Week 3 injuries to monitor:The Washington Commanders and Jayden Daniels got good news with the quarterback not requiring surgery on his injured elbow. General manager Adam Peters said Friday that an operation is "not on the table" and that they have not talked about placing Daniels on injured reserve, which would rule him out for at least four weeks.Nico Collins has been ruled out by the Houston Texans as he deals with a Grade 1 hamstring strain. Like Collins, Zay Flowers of the Baltimore Ravens also missed Week 2 and remained out of practice this week. He is listed as questionable for their game in Brazil.Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua sat out Friday's practice and is doubtful for Sunday night. Head coach Sean McVay said this week Nacua was "not making great progress" with the hip/groin issue that kept him out of Week 2. McVay added they expect Nacua to be ready to return next week.After being ruled out for the season with a knee injury, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart underwent surgery on Friday to repair his meniscus. According to The Athletic's Dan Duggan, Dart also suffered damage to his MCL and PCL, which will be addressed if needed. He is looking at a four-to-six month recovery period.Here's the rest of the Week 3 injury report:ARIZONA CARDINALSS Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (back): OUTDL Roy Lopez (groin): questionableCB Max Melton (toe): questionableBALTIMORE RAVENST Ronnie Stanley (toe): OUTWR Zay Flowers (hamstring): questionableBUFFALO BILLSDB Jordan Hancock (hamstring): OUTDL T.J. articles.title: College football scores, live updates: Oregon vs. USC, Texas A&M vs. LSU and more
articles.summary: After a wild first few weeks of the college football season, we may have our best slate yet in Week 4.
articles.body: After a wild first few weeks of the college football season, we may have our best slate yet in Week 4. Saturday features six matchups between teams ranked in the AP Top 25.The day started with a marquee showdown between No. 1 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee, and the Longhorns won rights to the 'UT' moniker with a tough defensive performance. Texas' Colin Simmons tied a school record with five sacks in a 20-17 win — though he did get in a bit of trouble after his first. No. 17 Iowa provided the drama for the day in the afternoon, driving the length of the field in the final minute and scoring on a walk-off TD pass from Hank Brown to Reece Vander Zee as time expired to beat No. 18 Michigan 20-19. Elsewhere, No. 4 Ole Miss got shelled by No. 21 Florida and No. 15 Utah held on for a 31-17 win at Iowa State.In the evening, we have a trifecta of ranked-on-ranked matchups with No. 23 Texas A&M vs. No. 10 LSU, No. 20 Oregon vs. No. 12 USC and No. 19 Missouri vs. No. 24 Mississippi State. It's an action-packed slate that surely won't disappoint.Follow all of the action with live updates, highlights and analysis below:

articles.title: AEW All Out 2026 live results: Updates, grades, analysis for Will Ospreay vs. Jon Moxley
articles.summary: Follow AEW All Out 2026 live results and match-by-match updates as AEW heads to Illinois with a stacked card, topped by the AEW World Championship match between Will Ospreay and Jon Moxley.
articles.body: AEW All Out 2026 follows AEW's historic night in London with another stacked show featuring seven title matches, headlined by the first defense of new world champion Will Ospreay. He'll be tasked with beating his latest mentor and the winningest AEW World Champion in company history, Jon Moxley. Follow AEW All Out 2026 live results, match-by-match updates, grades, winners and losers and more all day here with Uncrowned.Ospreay's coronation was a foregone conclusion in a home game at All In, after which the question quickly became: Who will challenge "The Aerial Assassin" first? Moxley, who won that same night, rose to the occasion, and now pursues yet another reign as AEW's lead man. Several story beats between the two have been strong since Ospreay's neck injury last year, and it all comes to a head in Saturday's All Out main event.Another title matchup likely to steal the show belongs to the tag-team division, where gold is up for grabs in a three-way ladder match. The champions, Cage and Cope, look to make even more history by replicating their famous TLC matches from the early 2000s; they'll be challenged by former AEW champions the Young Bucks and FTR.AEW International Champion Kazuchika Okada is additionally set to defend his title against Tommaso Ciampa in a true fantasy match. For years, the wrestlers couldn't have been farther apart from ever colliding; now, they'll go at it for Okada's AEW crown.Check out the full AEW All Out 2026 lineup below, which starts at 8 p.m. ET on HBO Max, Prime Video, PPV.com, Triller, Fite TV, Fubo, Sling TV, YouTube, DAZN (internationally) and MyAEW.com:AEW World Championship: Will Ospreay (c) vs. Jon MoxleyLadder Match for the AEW World Tag Team Championships: Cage and Cope (Christian Cage and Adam Copeland) (c) vs. FTR (Cash Wheeler and Dax Harwood) vs. The Young Bucks (Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson)AEW International Championship: Kazuchika Okada (c) vs. Tommaso CiampaAEW Women's World Tag Team Championship - Chicago Street Fight: The Brawling Birds (Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter) (c) vs. Divine Dominion (Lena Kross and Megan Bayne)AEW World Trios Championship: Swerve Strickland & The New Level (Austin Creed and Kofi) (c) vs. "Hangman" Adam Page & Brodido (Brody King and Bandido)AEW TBS Championship Open Challenge (Excluding Hyan, Maya World, and Thunder Rosa): Persephone (c) vs. TBAAEW Women's World Championship No. 1 Contender Match: Thekla vs. Willow NightingaleAEW World Tag Team Championship No. 1 Contender Match: Darby Allin and Steven Borden vs. The Don Callis Family (Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher)AEW National Championship: Andrade El Ídolo (c) def. articles.title: Takuma Inoue recovers from knockdown to repeat win over Tenshin Nasukawa in all-Japanese world title fight
articles.summary: Follow Takuma Inoue vs. Tenshin Nasukawa 2 live results and round-by-round updates for the Inoue vs. Nasukawa fight card on Sunday in Tokyo, Japan.
articles.body: Uncrowned has Takuma Inoue vs. Tenshin Nasukawa 2 live results, round-by-round updates, ring walks and start time for the Inoue vs. Nasukawa fight card on Sunday morning at Toyota Arena in Tokyo, Japan. Takuma Inoue defends his WBC bantamweight title in a rematch with Tenshin Nasukawa in the night's main event.Inoue (22-2, 5 KOs) is the brother of pound-for-pound king Naoya Inoue. He is a two-time bantamweight champion, having previously held the WBA title from 2023 to 2024. Inoue won the vacant WBC belt with a unanimous decision over Nasukawa in November 2025. He has fought once since, retaining his title with a decision over Kazuto Ioka in May.Nasukawa (8-1, 3 KOs) is widely hailed as one of the greatest kickboxers of all time. The Japanese superstar has also fought once since suffering his first career loss against Inoue, stopping Juan Francisco Estrada this past April.The Inoue vs. Nasukawa fight card begins at 4 a.m. ET and can be watched on DAZN. The main event ring walks are expected to take place around 7 a.m. ET.Follow all of the action with Uncrowned's live results and play-by-play of the fight card below.Fight card (4 a.m. ET, DAZN)WBC bantamweight title: Takuma Inoue def.
